transcript: Overthinking does not come from a broken mind. It comes from a lack of trust in the body. More precisely, you do not trust yourself to stay present with the uncomfortable feelings that might arise if your fears become real. So the mind looks for control. It plans. It imagines. It prepares for every possible outcome, not because you are weak, but because the body does not feel safe. The mind believes that if it thinks enough, it can protect you from pain. And so it catastrophizes, it strategizes, it rehearses every possible response. This is exhausting, and it never brings rest. Here is another way. Choose one action. Let it be simple. Let it be aligned with your values. Then take it. If things unfold as you hoped, continue gently. If they do not, continue gently, because the safety you are seeking does not live in controlling the world outside you. It lives in your ability to stay with yourself, to support your own body, and to remain present no matter how the moment unfolds. This is how trust is rebuilt, not through control, but through repeated self-support. If overthinking keeps you restless, my new e-book, The Way Back to Stillness, is in the link in my bio, not to fix you, but to help your body feel safe again.
